Gluten Free Chocolate Chip Muffins

Published: Aug 24, 2026 by Kim · This post may contain affiliate links · 2 Comments

Take classic chocolate chip muffins to the next level with brown butter! These gluten free muffins are tall, soft, and fluffy, packed with gooey chocolate chips, and filled with the irresistible nutty, caramel-like flavor of browned butter.

What's your favorite muffin flavor? Are you a banana muffin diehard? Or do you prefer the pops of fresh fruit in a blueberry muffin? While I love them both, my muffin of choice is—and probably always will be—a chocolate chip muffin. There's just something about adding chocolate that takes the humble little muffin from breakfast straight into almost-dessert territory. I can happily eat one for breakfast, grab one as an afternoon snack (they're perfect for kids coming home from school, by the way), or even choose one over a bowl of my favorite ice cream for dessert. A muffin that works for breakfast and dessert? That's my kind of muffin.

I didn't think a chocolate chip muffin needed improving...until I added brown butter. We all know butter makes everything better, right? But browning it takes that familiar sweet, creamy flavor and turns it into something altogether more irresistible. As the milk solids toast, they develop rich, nutty, almost caramel-like notes that become the perfect backdrop for all those melty chocolate chips. It's the kind of subtle flavor that makes you take another bite and wonder why these muffins taste so much better than any chocolate chip muffin you've had before.

Ingredients needed

  • Kim's gluten free all purpose flour blend — my flour blend gives these muffins their soft, fluffy texture and tender crumb. A store-bought gluten free flour blend may work as a substitute, but I haven’t tested one in this recipe.
  • Buttermilk — look for whole milk buttermilk if you can find it. The extra richness and acidity help create incredibly soft, fluffy muffins with a tender crumb.
  • Sour cream — one of my favorite ingredients for adding moisture and richness without making muffins heavy. Full-fat Greek yogurt can be substituted with similar results.
  • Mini chocolate chips — I prefer mini chocolate chips because they disperse throughout the batter, giving you little pockets of melty chocolate in every single bite. Feel free to use regular chocolate chips if that’s what you have on hand.
  • Butter — these aren’t just chocolate chip muffins—they’re brown butter chocolate chip muffins! Browning the butter transforms it into something rich, nutty, and almost caramel-like, adding incredible depth of flavor. Use the real stuff, y’all!

Making the best chocolate chip muffins

  1. Step 1: Melt butter in a small saucepan until the foam begins to subside and the milk solids turn brown. Immediately remove from the heat and pour into a large bowl to cool briefly.
  1. Step 2: Add eggs, oil, and sugar to the slightly cooled brown butter and whisk to combine.
  1. Step 3: Add buttermilk, sour cream, and vanilla and whisk to combine.
  1. Step 4: Whisk together flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt and fold this into the batter. Lumps are okay.
  1. Step 5: Fold in chocolate chips. Cover and let sit for 15 minutes.
  1. Step 6: Scoop batter all the way to the top (and a little over) of every other muffin hole (you should get 6 muffins per muffin pan).
  1. Step 7: If desired, sprinkle demerara or turbinado sugar on top of each muffin.
  1. Step 8: Bake at 425F for 7 minutes, then reduce the temperature to 350F and continue to bake for another 12-15 minutes, or until they spring back when lightly touched.

Gluten free chocolate chip muffins FAQs

What does brown butter do to muffins?

Brown butter adds a rich, nutty, almost caramel-like flavor that regular melted butter just can’t match. Browning the butter toasts the milk solids, creating all those wonderful deeper flavors while still giving the muffins the richness and tenderness you expect from butter.

Why are my gluten free muffins dry?

The most common culprits are too much flour or overbaking. For the best results, weigh your gluten free flour rather than measuring it by volume, and begin checking your muffins toward the end of the suggested baking time. Gluten free baked goods can go from perfectly moist to dry surprisingly quickly.

How do I get tall, bakery-style muffin tops?

A thicker batter, properly leavened dough, and the right oven temperature all help create those beautiful tall muffin tops. Make sure you fill the muffin wells all the way to the top (even a little over that is good). Initially starting the muffins in a hot oven (425F) allows them to rise tall and bakery-like. Only fill 6 muffin wells per muffin pan, so each muffin has plenty of space to expand as needed. All of these ensure great success in bakery-style muffin baking!

Gluten Free Chocolate Chip Muffins

Course: Breakfast
Cuisine: American
Keyword: chocolate chip, Gluten Free, muffins
Prep Time: 15 minutes minutes
Cook Time: 22 minutes minutes
Servings: 12 muffins
Author: Kim
Take classic chocolate chip muffins to the next level with brown butter! These gluten free muffins are tall, soft, and fluffy, packed with gooey chocolate chips, and filled with the irresistible nutty, caramel-like flavor of browned butter.
Print Recipe Pin Recipe Cook Mode

Equipment

  • 2 muffin pan

Ingredients

  • 6 tbsp (85g) butter
  • 2½ cups (350g) Kim's gluten free all purpose flour blend (a store bought blend may be substituted, but hasn't been tested)
  • 2½ teaspoon baking powder
  • ½ teaspoon baking soda
  • ½ teaspoon kosher salt
  • ¼ cup (60g) avocado oil (or any neutral oil of choice)
  • 1 cup (200g) granulated sugar
  • 2 large eggs, at room temperature
  • 1¼ cups (300g) whole milk buttermilk, at room temperature (or 1½ tablespoon of vinegar or lemon juice mixed with 1¼ cups of milk of choice, preferably high fat milk)
  • ½ cup (120g) sour cream, at room temperature (or Greek yogurt)
  • 1 tablespoon vanilla bean paste or extract
  • 1¼ cups (230g) mini chocolate chips
  • turbinado or demerara sugar, for sprinkling (if desired)

Instructions

  • Preheat the oven to 425℉. Line a 12-cup muffin pan with 6 paper muffin liners (to achieve the classic bakery style, only fill every other muffin well so that each muffin has a chance to rise high). Set aside.
  • Brown the butter: Add the butter to a small saucepan or skillet and heat over medium heat. Allow to melt and continually swirl the pan or still until the milk solids begin to fall to the bottom and brown (about 5 minutes). Remove from heat and pour into a large bowl; let cool slightly.
  • In a medium bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt; set aside.
  • After the brown butter has cooled slightly, add the oil, sugar, and eggs to it and whisk to combine. Then add the sour cream (or Greek yogurt), buttermilk, and vanilla and whisk well until the mixture is pale yellow.
  • Add the dry ingredients to the wet and stir to combine and then fold in the mini chocolate chips. Cover and let sit for 15 minutes. Don't skip this step as it properly hydrates the flour and allows the batter to absorb the fluids appropriately.
  • Divide the batter between the lined muffin cups, filling all the way to the top (almost to the point of overfilling). Sprinkle with turbinado or demerara sugar.
  • Bake at 425℉ for 7 minutes, then reduce the temperature to 350℉ and continue to bake for another 12-15 minutes, until the tops are golden brown and they bounce back when lightly touched. A toothpick inserted into the center should come out clean or with just a few moist crumbs.
  • Remove from the oven and allow to sit in the muffin pan for 10 minutes before removing to cooling rack to cool further.
  • Muffins can be enjoyed slightly warm or at room temperature, with or without butter and flaky sea salt (try the salt, it really balances the sweetness from the chocolate!).

Notes

Muffins will keep at room temperature, well wrapped, for up to 4 days. For longer storage, place in an airtight container or ziploc bag and freeze for up to 3 months. 

Adapted from Well Made by Kiley
